title: Python: the walker misses two binding kinds (PEP 695 'type m = ...' and 'with ctx() as (m, n)' tuple targets), so a name looks unbound
description: Found by the Opus review of #159 (GCLI-100, D1) at 29c775e5, PRE-EXISTING (wrong-edge direction: a binding is missed, so a name looks unbound or singly bound). Probed by the worker on dev abea54f with class B: def m; class C(B): <body>; C().m(): (1) class body 'type m = int' (PEP 695 type alias statement): the walker records no binding, so C().m() still gets an edge to B.m (1 edge; control 'm = None' gives 0); (2) class body 'with ctx() as (m, n): pass': addAsPatternBinding takes only direct identifier children (calls.ts around 1035-1045), so the tuple target binds nothing and the edge to B.m is kept (1 edge). Both make a name look unbound where Python binds it, and every single-binding rule (E1, N3, D1 and the bare-call enumeration) relies on the walker. Match capture patterns are GCLI-101 (D2), not here. Not built: routed to opum-doc through the leader first. Probe first for further forms (with-as list targets, nested tuples, starred), then red-before fixtures per hole, fix, mutation checks, per-site re-measure of the five pins.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a class-body type alias statement and a with-as tuple (or list, nested, starred) target are each recorded as a binding, with red-before fixtures
each hole has a mutation check that goes red
a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it removes named

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a35)). PROBE FIRST on dev 940e77e, class B: def m; class C(B): <body>; C().m(), edges to B.m (control m = None: 0). HOLES (1 edge kept, should be 0): type m = int; type m[T] = list[T]; with ctx() as (m, n); [m, n]; (a, (m, b)); (a, *m); [a, *m]; (ctx() as (m, n)) parenthesised; a second item after a plain one. NOT holes: with ctx() as m.x (an attribute target binds no name; 1, correct), with-as plain name and with a, b forms (0 already), def zz[m] (a type parameter binds in its own scope; 1, correct), del m and m: int unchanged. Parser shapes (tree-sitter-python): type_alias_statement left: type > identifier, or type > generic_type > identifier + type_parameter; a with-as target is as_pattern > as_pattern_target > (identifier | tuple | list), with a starred element spelled list_splat (not list_splat_pattern). FIX in calls.ts: a type_alias_statement arm in the walker binds the left name (rebound); addAsPatternBinding now runs addTargetBindings over the target so tuple, list, nested and attribute forms are handled by the one existing path, and addTargetBindings accepts list_splat. FIXTURES (test/python-calls.test.ts, D1 describe): 12 hole shapes x m and __call__ x four lookup shapes expect no edge (control m = None among them), and twins: type other, with ... as (a, b), [a, *b], and attribute or subscript targets NAME.x, (a, NAME.x), a[NAME] still reach the base. RED BEFORE: the hole test fails on the dev source, the twin test passes. MUTATION CHECKS, 5 mutants each red (source restored): type alias binding off, generic-type descent off, with-as identifier-only, list_splat off, type alias dispatch off; none survived. PER-SITE MEASURE, instrumented origin/dev 940e77e vs the branch, five pins, multiset diff, entry counts equal: ZERO changed sites on flask (3961), jinja (6159), httpx (4189), rich (9844), tqdm (3107): no bin moves, no in-repo edge created or removed. NOT MEASURED: precision, anything beyond the five pins. Gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test 828 pass.

REVIEW ROUND 1 (Opus, #162 at 3583bd43), amends the build note above: (B1) a parenthesised single-name with-as target was a real hole the first probe missed: 'with ctx() as (m):', '(a, (m))', '((m))' and '[a, (m)]' kept the edge to B.m (a tree-sitter parenthesized_expression, which addTargetBindings did not recurse into); fixed with a parenthesized_expression arm, and all four are in the hole table. (F1) twins added for 'def zz[m]', 'type other[NAME] = list[NAME]' (a type parameter binds in its own scope) and 'as (a, (b))'. MUTANTS now 7, each red: type alias binding off, generic-type descent off, with-as identifier-only, list_splat off, parenthesized_expression off, bind every identifier under left, type alias dispatch off (the build note said 5). Per-site measure re-run: 0 changed sites on the five pins, entry counts equal. Gates: bun test 828 pass.
